title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.17030v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The massive overactuation in the human musculoskeletal system makes it challenging to train musculoskeletal models to generate human-like motion via reinforcement learning, primarily because exploration in the resulting high-dimensional and redundant action space is extremely inefficient. To address this problem, we propose the $\lambda$-hold controller, inspired by the equilibrium-point (EP) hypothesis, which has been widely supported by extensive evidence from human motor control studies. The policy's control variable is the per-muscle EP threshold length $\lambda$, from which a stretch-reflex recruitment law computes the muscle excitations automatically. Holding each $\lambda$ over an interval of the gait phase also sharply reduces the frequency at which the policy must be queried. Consequently, the controller, to our knowledge for the first time, enables a muscle-actuated skeletal model to learn human-like sprinting using only a mi

translated_title: λ-保持控制：预测性肌肉骨骼模拟中从最小任务奖励涌现出类人运动
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17030v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：人体肌肉骨骼系统中的大量过度驱动使得通过强化学习训练肌肉骨骼模型生成类人运动变得具有挑战性，主要原因是在高维且冗余的动作空间中进行探索极其低效。为解决这一问题，我们提出了λ-保持控制器，其灵感来源于平衡点（EP）假说，该假说已被人类运动控制研究中的大量证据广泛支持。策略的控制变量是每条肌肉的平衡点阈值长度λ，由此，一种牵张反射募集法则自动计算肌肉兴奋。在步态相位的间隔内保持每个λ不变，也显著降低了策略需要被查询的频率。因此，据我们所知，该控制器首次使得肌肉驱动的骨骼模型仅通过最小任务奖励就能学习类人冲刺运动。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于平衡点假说的λ-保持控制器，通过控制肌肉阈值长度并降低策略查询频率，首次实现了仅用最小任务奖励让肌肉骨骼模型学习类人冲刺运动。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a λ-hold controller inspired by the equilibrium-point hypothesis, which reduces policy query frequency and enables, for the first time, a muscle-actuated skeletal model to learn human-like sprinting with only a minimal task reward.
